# Grammarly vs Alternatives: Best Writing Assistant 2026

Grammarly is the default writing checker, but it is not the only option. The question is which alternative fits your job: long-form, SEO, translation, or pure proofing, before you pay for the wrong plan

## The decision before you

The comparison only makes sense once you know what you are optimising for. Cost is not the main filter here: 7 are free or freemium. What separates them is how much setup you will tolerate and whether they fit what you already publish. 2 are paid-only. Read for the limits rather than the features, and pick the tool that fits one job you do often

## The tools worth considering

### Grammarly

[[link:/tools/90|Grammarly]] is a Freemium writing tool for Content Creation, Beginners, Quick Results. It handles email Polish and Draft Rewrites, and its key strength is that works almost anywhere through browser extension and keyboard-level integration. The honest limit: some regions may need VPN workarounds for full feature availability

### Jasper

[[link:/tools/18|Jasper]] is a Paid writing tool for Teams, Marketing, High Quality. It handles brand Campaigns and Long-Form SEO, and its key strength is that brand Voice training keeps large teams aligned on tone and terminology. The honest limit: paid-only pricing with per-seat costs is expensive for individuals

### SurferSEO

[[link:/tools/57|SurferSEO]] is a Paid writing tool for Content Creation, Beginners, Quick Results. It handles content Scoring and Structure Guidance, and its key strength is that real-time scoring gives concrete targets while the draft is being written. The honest limit: access may require VPN in some regions outside supported countries

### Poe

[[link:/tools/73|Poe]] is a Freemium writing tool for Content Creation, Beginners, Quick Results. It handles model Comparison and Custom Bots, and its key strength is that many models accessible from one app and account. The honest limit: heavy use of some models is limited by subscription quotas

### DeepL Write

[[link:/tools/99|DeepL Write]] is a Freemium writing tool for Content Creation, Beginners, Quick Results. It handles text Polishing and Tone Adjustment, and its key strength is that tone, style and formality controls give precise rewrite direction. The honest limit: access is restricted in some regions and may need a VPN

### ProWritingAid

[[link:/tools/205|ProWritingAid]] is a Freemium writing tool for Editing, Authors, Readability. It handles manuscript Editing and Academic Writing, and its key strength is that style reports go deeper than grammar into pacing and sentence variety. The honest limit: advanced style reports and longer checks require paid subscriptions

### Wordtune

[[link:/tools/1531|Wordtune]] is a Freemium writing tool for Writers, Professionals, Students. It handles sentence Rewrites and Tone Shifts, and its key strength is that suggestion-as-you-type works inside browsers and common writing surfaces. The honest limit: free plan limits the number of daily rewrites and modes

### QuillBot

[[link:/tools/24|QuillBot]] is a Freemium writing tool for Content Creation, Beginners, Quick Results. It handles paraphrasing Text and Summaries, and its key strength is that multiple paraphrase modes let users adjust tone without rewriting by hand. The honest limit: access can be restricted in some regions, sometimes requiring VPN use

### LanguageTool

[[link:/tools/1439|LanguageTool]] is a Freemium writing tool for Writers who need AI-powered grammar checking with multilingual support. It handles multilingual Checking and Email Proofing, and its key strength is that supports over 30 languages including German, French, Spanish, and Dutch. The honest limit: free version limits text length and number of advanced style checks

## How to choose

Start where the friction is highest. If you are unsure, begin with [[link:/tools/90|Grammarly]] and [[link:/tools/18|Jasper]], since they cover the common cases and are forgiving to learn. Expand one tool at a time, when a specific job has repeated often enough to earn it. Do not upgrade until you can name the specific limit you hit in the free version

## A workflow you can chain today

Draft in [[link:/tools/18|Jasper]], proof in [[link:/tools/90|Grammarly]], translate tone in [[link:/tools/99|DeepL Write]], and score SEO copy with [[link:/tools/57|SurferSEO]]

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Treating AI output as final. Every tool here produces something that needs checking before it reaches an audience.
- Ignoring skill level. A tool that assumes an advanced workflow sits unused if you do not have one.
- Stacking too many subscriptions. Two tools that do the same job are one too many, and the free tiers are enough to find out.
- Skipping verification. These tools produce plausible output, and plausible is not the same as correct

## FAQ

### Is Grammarly enough on its own?

For general proofing, often yes; for SEO or translation, add [[link:/tools/57|SurferSEO]] or [[link:/tools/99|DeepL Write]]

### Which alternative is best for writers?

[[link:/tools/205|ProWritingAid]] and [[link:/tools/1531|Wordtune]] offer deeper rewriting than basic checks

### Do I need a multilingual tool?

[[link:/tools/99|DeepL Write]] and [[link:/tools/1439|LanguageTool]] handle multiple languages and tone

### What should I not outsource?

Final accountability for meaning; check suggestions rather than accepting all

## Final takeaway

The setups that hold up assign a tool to each stage and keep a human check on the result. Start with the options closest to your task and let usage decide what joins them.

mainEntity.name: What does Grammarly actually do that a general AI assistant does not?

acceptedAnswer.text: Grammarly is built around correctness — grammar, clarity, tone and consistency wherever you type. A general assistant can do the same checks when asked, but it is not embedded in your editor, so you have to move your text to it. If your problem is fixing what you already wrote, Grammarly is the faster loop.

mainEntity.name: When would I choose an alternative over Grammarly?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you need generation rather than correction. A general-purpose assistant writes longer-form first drafts and answers questions about your own documents, which Grammarly is not designed for. If most of your time goes on producing text rather than fixing it, a different tool is the better fit.

mainEntity.name: Is Grammarly Premium worth paying for?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how much you write for work. The free tier catches basic grammar and spelling; Premium adds the clarity, tone and consistency suggestions that matter in client-facing and professional writing. If you send text to clients or publish under a brand voice, it is usually worth it — otherwise the free tier covers most people.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Grammarly alongside a separate AI writing tool?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and many people do: one tool to draft, one to polish. Just run the polishing pass last so you are proofreading the final text rather than an intermediate draft you are about to rewrite.

tldr: Match the checker to your job: proofing, SEO, or multilingual tone.
